papers.abstract: The optimal duration of follow-up for patients with follicular lymphoma (FL) eligible for initial watch-and-wait (WAW) remains undefined. We investigated the clinical characteristics and treatment trajectory patterns in patients with FL managed by initial, continuous WAW for at least 5 years (WAW5). Patients were identified from The Danish National Lymphoma Registry and detailed information was collected from health care records. Among the 393 included WAW5-patients, 271 (69%) were still untreated after a median follow-up of 5.3 years (after WAW5-timepoint). The 2-, 5-, and 10-year cumulative incidences of treatment initiation were 16% (95% CI 12%-20%), 28% (95% CI 24%-33%) and 38% (95% CI 32%-44%), respectively. In patients with stage II-IV disease, the best subset selection method in the training cohort (7:3 random sampling) identified the multivariable Cox regression model with number of nodal areas and bone marrow involvement with the best prognostic fit for time to treatment (TTT). Based on this, the WAW5-TTT risk score was constructed. The 5-year cumulative incidence of treatment initiation in the training cohort was 46% (95% CI 35%-58%), 37% (95% CI 26%-48%), and 13% (95% CI 5%-21%) in the high-, intermediate, and low-risk WAW5-TTT groups, respectively (Gray's test p < 0.0001). Results were confirmed in the test cohort. In conclusion, most patients remained treatment-free beyond the WAW5-timepoint. The findings support consideration of discontinuation of routine follow-up or transition to a more flexible, need-driven follow-up after WAW5, with the option of incorporating relevant risk factors to support individualized decision-making.

papers.abstract: Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) is a multifunctional protein that participates in cancer metabolism, apoptosis, DNA repair, angiogenesis, and immune regulation beyond its canonical glycolytic role. However, how distinct post-translational modifications (PTMs) coordinate GAPDH functional transitions and determine its diverse biological roles in cancer remains incompletely understood. In this review, we summarize current advances in GAPDH PTMs, including methylation, phosphorylation, acetylation, ubiquitination, S-nitrosylation, serotonylation, crotonylation, lactylation, and succinylation, with emphasis on modification sites, regulatory enzymes, cellular contexts, and functional consequences. We propose a PTM-driven molecular switching model in which different cellular stimuli induce specific GAPDH modifications to regulate its enzymatic activity, subcellular localization, and protein interactions. Representative mechanisms include Src-mediated Tyr41 phosphorylation promoting DNA repair and 5-fluorouracil resistance in colorectal cancer, K254 and K160 acetylation regulating glycolytic activity and apoptosis through distinct cellular contexts, Parkin-mediated ubiquitination controlling mitophagy and metabolic reprogramming, and Gln262 serotonylation enhancing CD8+ T-cell glycolytic function and antitumor immunity. We further discuss the crosstalk among GAPDH PTMs and critically evaluate the current evidence, limitations, and therapeutic implications of GAPDH modification-based regulation. Although GAPDH PTMs represent promising targets for cancer intervention, current evidence is mainly derived from cellular and preclinical models, and PTM-specific therapeutic strategies remain limited. Further studies are required to clarify the cancer-specific functions and clinical relevance of GAPDH PTM networks.

papers.abstract: Influenza viruses and coronaviruses are enveloped, single-stranded RNA viruses that pose persistent and pandemic threats to global public health. Despite belonging to distinct viral families, they share remarkable parallels in modes of transmission, clinical manifestations, and socioeconomic impacts, yet diverge fundamentally in evolutionary mechanisms and epidemiological trajectories. This review compares the history, spread, treatments, and vaccines for these two types of viruses. Influenza viruses possess a segmented genome, which enables antigenic shift and reassortment. In contrast, coronaviruses have large, nonsegmented genomes and rely on recombination, mutation accumulation, and insertions to achieve host switching and immune evasion. Both spread to humans through wildlife (intermediate hosts), live animal markets, intensive agriculture, and global travel. Antiviral strategies have evolved from M2 and neuraminidase inhibitors (NAIs) for influenza to polymerase inhibitors and protease inhibitors for coronavirus, yet drug resistance remains a common challenge. Vaccine platforms, including inactivated, live-attenuated, recombinant, mRNA, and viral vector technologies, have been deployed against both viruses. This review concludes that integrated, platform-based preparedness, encompassing broad-spectrum antivirals, universal vaccines, and proactive ecological surveillance, is essential for building pandemic-resilient public health systems capable of responding to both influenza and coronavirus threats, as well as future emerging respiratory viruses.

papers.abstract: Cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) during total aortic arch replacement (TAR) is associated with coagulopathy. We investigated whether fresh frozen plasma (FFP) administration during CPB was associated with postoperative transfusion requirements and coagulation profiles after TAR. This single-center retrospective cohort study included adult patients who underwent elective TAR. Patients were categorized according to whether FFP was administered during CPB. The primary outcome was postoperative FFP transfusion from CPB separation to 12 h after intensive care unit admission. Secondary outcomes included perioperative plasma-derived product use, postoperative bleeding, re-exploration for bleeding, and serial coagulation parameters. Multivariable regression analyses were performed to adjust for potential confounders. Data from 156 patients were analyzed, including 111 patients in the Pre-FFP group and 45 in the Control group. Baseline characteristics were generally comparable, although deep hypothermic circulatory arrest duration and CPB fluid management differed between the groups. The adjusted mean difference in total post-CPB FFP transfusion units between the Pre-FFP and Control groups was - 1.54 units (95% confidence interval, - 7.51 to 4.43). No significant differences were observed in perioperative plasma-derived product use or bleeding outcomes. Although fibrinogen concentrations were higher and activated partial thromboplastin time and prothrombin time-international normalized ratio were shorter at the end of CPB in the Pre-FFP group, these differences largely resolved after CPB. FFP administration during CPB was associated with transient improvement in coagulation parameters but was not associated with postoperative transfusion requirements or bleeding outcomes in adult patients undergoing elective TAR. Larger studies are needed to confirm these findings.

papers.abstract: Tumor necrosis is associated with poor prognosis in colorectal cancer (CRC) yet is generally viewed as a passive consequence of tumor growth rather than a therapeutic target. We demonstrate that necrosis correlates with metastatic disease in human CRC independently of tumor size. Single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics of primary CRC and colorectal liver metastases revealed that peri-necrotic programs are associated with metastatic progression. Patients with CRC exhibited increased circulating neutrophils, including NET-primed and CD177-low neutrophils with reduced extravasation capacity. Consistent with these findings, intravascular NET aggregates localized adjacent to necrotic regions in human CRC specimens. In a mismatch repair-proficient mouse model of CRC, neutrophil infiltration and NET formation increased during tumor progression, whereas genetic and pharmacologic NET inhibition reduced tumor necrosis, decreased metastasis, and enhanced chemotherapy efficacy. Together, these findings identify NET-driven tumor necrosis as an active promoter of CRC metastasis and support NET inhibition as a therapeutic strategy.

papers.abstract: Obesity is a well-established risk factor for multiple myeloma (MM), yet the burden attributable to high body mass index (BMI) in BRICS countries remains unclear. This study assessed temporal trends, regional variations, and future projections of this burden. Data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 study were used to estimate the incidence, mortality, prevalence, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) of MM attributable to high BMI during 1990-2023 across Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa. Age-period-cohort modeling, joinpoint regression, decomposition analysis, and Bayesian age-period-cohort forecasting were applied to evaluate trends and project the burden through 2040. Globally, deaths and DALYs increased substantially during 1990-2023, while age-standardized rates increased more modestly. Considerable heterogeneity was observed across BRICS countries. India showed the most rapid long-term increase, China accounted for the largest absolute burden in 2023, and South Africa exhibited among the highest age-standardized rates, whereas the Russian Federation showed a recent declining trend. Decomposition analysis indicated that population growth was the predominant contributor to the global increase, while epidemiological change represented the major contributor in China and India. Age-period-cohort analysis demonstrated that the burden was concentrated among older populations, with increasing risks observed in more recent periods and birth cohorts, particularly in countries undergoing rapid epidemiological transitions. BAPC projections suggested continued increases in the global burden and in most BRICS countries through 2040, whereas declining trends were projected for the Russian Federation. Sex-specific analyses showed a consistently higher burden among men, although sex differences varied across regions. The high BMI-related MM burden in BRICS countries is rising, with distinct regional patterns driven by demographic expansion and changing risk profiles. Targeted obesity prevention, cancer surveillance, and equitable access to MM diagnosis and treatment may help mitigate the future MM burden.

papers.abstract: Retrospective studies and analyses of RCTs showed that surgical quality of mesorectal excision affects oncological outcomes of rectal cancer patients. Objective of this study was to determine the impact of mesorectal excision quality on local recurrence and overall survival in rectal cancer patients. MEDLINE was searched till April 1, 2024, with MeSH terms: rectal cancer/neoplasm, total mesorectal excision, TME, rectal cancer surgery, macroscopic assessment/evaluation, quality/adequacy/completeness of surgery/mesorectum/resection specimen, prognosis, and outcome for randomized clinical trials, prospective and retrospective cohort studies reporting oncological outcomes and quality of the mesorectal excision. The main outcome and measures were local recurrence and overall survival. TME quality was classified into three grading categories (complete or mesorectal resection (MRR); nearly complete or intramesorectal resection (IMR); incomplete or muscularis propria resection (MPR)). Of 438 records screened and an additional three studies by cross-referencing, 15 articles with 11,285 individual patients were identified. Median age of included patients was 63, 55 (range 21, 0-95, 0). Pooled incidence of good (MRR), intermediate (IMR), and insufficient (MPR) TME quality was 65, 6%, 22, 8%, and 11, 6%, respectively. Insufficient TME quality was associated with locally advanced tumors. No difference in TME quality was observed between patients with and without neoadjuvant therapy. Pooled analysis showed lower odds for LR and higher odds for OS in patients with good TME quality, which is also shown in a subgroup analysis of neoadjuvantly treated patients. In conclusion, this meta-analysis confirms that good TME quality is associated with lower risk for local recurrence and higher probability for overall survival, an association that persisted also in neoadjuvantly treated patients. These findings suggest that neoadjuvant therapy will not compensate for suboptimal surgical quality; however, given the substantial heterogeneity across the included studies and the limited availability of data on contemporary treatment regimens, they should be regarded as hypothesis-generating rather than definitive.

papers.abstract: People with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV; hereafter, PWH) face differences in cancer treatment and quality. In a cross-sectional survey (December 2022-August 2025) of 120 PWH diagnosed with cancer and receiving care at an NCI-designated comprehensive cancer center in Florida, we examined associations of HIV stigma (Berger HIV Stigma Scale) and everyday discrimination (Everyday Discrimination Scale) with cancer care quality (Consumer Assessment of Healthcare Providers and Systems [CAHPS], Patient-Centered Communication in Cancer Care [PCCC], Health Care System Distrust, and Barriers to Care scales). Multivariable linear regression models were adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics and cancer type. Personalized stigma was associated with lower PCCC fostering healthy relationships (β: -0.29; 95% CI: -0.56, -0.01). Disclosure concerns were associated with worse care coordination (β: -0.23; 95% CI: -0.46, -0.01), greater distrust (β: 0.23; 95% CI: 0.05, 0.41), and greater barriers to care (β: 0.19; 95% CI: 0.01, 0.38). Everyday discrimination was associated with lower global healthcare ratings (β: -0.41; 95% CI: -0.71, -0.11). This is the first quantitative evidence that HIV stigma, particularly disclosure-related facets, undermined measurable cancer care quality.

papers.abstract: Extrachromosomal circular DNA (eccDNA) is an essential type of circular DNA that is mainly characterized by independence from chromosomes and a broad size distribution. Increasing evidence suggests that the distinctive genomic distribution of eccDNA establishes it as a clinical biomarker. Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms underlying its biogenesis and function in tumorigenesis have not been fully elucidated. Thus, in this review, we summarize the emerging insights into the biogenesis mechanisms of eccDNA, with particular emphasis on the recently described single-strand break driven internal loop (i-loop) model. We also discuss its critical roles in oncogenesis, including oncogene amplification, tumor heterogeneity, cell death, tumor immunity and drug resistance. We further outline current detection methods for eccDNA and evaluate its potential as a promising diagnostic, prognostic and predictive biomarker for human cancers, as well as a therapeutic vulnerability with implications for chemotherapy, radiotherapy, immunotherapy and nanotherapy.

papers.abstract: Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) analysis provides a minimally invasive approach to breast cancer assessment across early detection, minimal residual disease (MRD) monitoring, and treatment adaptation in advanced disease. This review evaluates these applications by distinguishing analytical validity, clinical detection performance, prognostic validity, and clinical utility. In early detection, assays integrating genomic, epigenomic, fragmentomic, and protein-based features have shown encouraging performance in evaluated cohorts; however, sensitivity remains limited in low-burden disease, particularly stage I breast cancer. Their potential clinical role depends on the incremental information they provide beyond established imaging and diagnostic pathways. In the curative-intent setting, circulating tumor DNA detection after treatment is associated with recurrence risk and can precede clinical or radiographic relapse, supporting prognostic stratification and the design of MRD-guided intervention trials. Whether such interventions improve clinical outcomes remains a central unresolved question. In advanced breast cancer, plasma genotyping supports treatment selection in defined molecular contexts. Randomized trials of ESR1 mutation-guided endocrine switching have demonstrated progression-free survival benefits with specific treatment strategies, providing evidence beyond biomarker-outcome associations, although overall survival benefit remains to be established. Across applications, interpretation depends on assay characteristics, molecular input, disease setting, sampling schedule, and the clinical decision being evaluated. Future studies should connect assay performance to patient benefit through comparison with existing care, clinically meaningful endpoints, and assessment of treatment burden and downstream investigations. This approach will help define where cfDNA testing can contribute meaningfully to breast cancer management.

papers.abstract: Ciltacabtagene autoleucel (cilta-cel) is a B cell maturation-antigen-targeting chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell product approved for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma treatment. Previously reported cases of post-cilta-cel immune effector cell enterocolitis (IEC-EC) have been described as a severe diarrhea associated with clonal CAR T cell populations. Here we report nine cases of cilta-cel-associated IEC-EC with CAR T cell-positive (CAR+) infiltration in 158 cilta-cel-treated patients at MD Anderson Cancer Center (incidence of 5.1% at a 6-month landmark and 5.7% globally). Cilta-cel infiltration was the primary cause of IEC-EC, and all cases demonstrated monoclonal or oligoclonal T cell populations as measured by vector integration analysis, flow cytometry and T cell receptor sequencing. Patients with IEC-EC had 100-fold more CAR T cell persistence in the peripheral blood than patients without IEC-EC. RNA sequencing analysis revealed increased cytotoxic and inflammatory programs associated with the CAR+ infiltrates relative to controls. Clonal vector integration occurred in introns of highly expressed genes without evidence of vector-mediated mutagenesis. Candidate driver mutations were sparse and heterogeneous, distinguishing IEC-EC from peripheral T cell lymphoma following CAR T cell therapy. In sum, we find that IEC-EC pathology represents a distinct, duodenum-predominant, clonal lymphoproliferative disorder characterized by the infiltration of clonal CAR+ cytotoxic T cells into the gastrointestinal tract.

papers.abstract: Metastases arise when cancer cells disseminate from the primary tumor, or other metastases, and seed tumors at distant anatomical sites. Reconstructing migration histories from DNA sequencing data is key to understanding the cellular mechanisms underlying metastatic dissemination. While the data often support many equally plausible histories, current methods return a single solution or sample alternatives without guarantees of optimality or completeness. Here we introduce MACH2, which enumerates all optimal migration histories and summarizes them to identify high-confidence migrations. MACH2 combines existing parsimony criteria with a new criterion that minimizes the number of clones assigned to locations where they were not observed, and includes MACH2-viz, an interactive tool for exploring solutions. Using simulated tumors with known ground truth, we show that MACH2 outperforms existing methods. Across 145 lung, ovarian, breast and prostate cancers, MACH2 reveals extensive uncertainty in migration histories, infers histories consistent with orthogonal experimental data, and finds metastasis-to-metastasis seeding and linear progression to be common.

papers.abstract: Long-term survival after definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy (dCCRT) remains limited in locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). We evaluated induction immunochemotherapy followed by dCCRT and consolidation immunotherapy in this setting. This prospective, single-arm Phase II study enrolled 54 adults selected for definitive nonsurgical treatment. The planned regimen comprised two cycles of induction immunochemotherapy with nab-paclitaxel, carboplatin, and a programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) inhibitor, followed by dCCRT with 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions and concurrent weekly chemotherapy. The same PD-1 inhibitor was planned as consolidation therapy for up to 1 year. The primary endpoint was the 2-year overall survival (OS) rate. Fifty-three patients (98.1%) completed two induction cycles, all 54 proceeded to dCCRT, and 31 (57.4%) received consolidation immunotherapy. Among all 54 enrolled patients, the 2-year OS and progression-free survival (PFS) rates were 84.6% (95% confidence interval [CI], 75.2%-95.0%) and 61.5% (95% CI, 49.5%-76.4%), respectively, after a median follow-up of 28.1 months. Adverse events occurred predominantly during dCCRT and were mainly hematologic; lymphopenia and esophagitis were among the most frequent toxicities. Exploratory analyses suggested that suboptimal response after induction immunochemotherapy was associated with shorter PFS. The survival outcomes observed with this sequential approach support further evaluation of its comparative clinical benefit in randomized studies. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05621707).

papers.abstract: Immune effector cell-associated enterocolitis (IEC-EC) is a delayed toxicity of ciltacabtagene autoleucel. The US Multiple Myeloma Immunotherapy Consortium retrospectively adjudicated 54 suspected cases from 8 institutions: 41 were IEC-EC (31 confirmed by anti-camelid variable heavy-chain immunohistochemistry, 10 probable). Through September 2025, cumulative incidence was 3.0% (39 of 1,308 ciltacabtagene autoleucel recipients; 95% CI 2.1-4.1%); 12-month competing-risk incidence was 3.0% (95% CI 2.1-4.1%). Median symptom onset was 75 days after infusion. Grade ≥3 diarrhea occurred in 85% (34 of 40 with diarrhea); 73% (30 of 41) required parenteral nutrition. Despite normal upper endoscopy in 41% (9 of 22), duodenal biopsies showed villous blunting, apoptotic bodies and a dense cytotoxic T cell infiltrate, CD4+ in 61% (19 of 31), CD8+ in 26% (8 of 31) and mixed in 13% (4 of 31). A dominant T cell clone was detected in 76% (13 of 17 tested). Delayed neurotoxicity co-occurred in 41% (17 of 41). At last follow-up, 32% (13 of 41) resolved, 27% (11 of 41) had ongoing symptoms and 41% (17 of 41) died with active IEC-EC. Combined biologic and T cell-directed therapy yielded the highest resolution (55%, 6 of 11) in small subgroups. IEC-EC is potentially fatal and requires systematic evaluation and early directed therapy.

papers.abstract: Radiotherapy is uniquely vulnerable during armed conflicts because it depends on immovable equipment, trained staff, daily patient travel, reliable infrastructure, and uninterrupted access to treatment records. We describe the experience of the Department of Radiation Oncology at the American University of Beirut during two episodes of intense conflict affecting Lebanon in 2024 and 2026. We specifically focus on the closure of a satellite clinic and how we managed the resumption of care for displaced patients. Based on this experience, we propose practical preparedness measures for radiotherapy services in conflict-prone regions, including live off-site patient registries, predefined transfer workflows, regional radiotherapy capacity mapping, triage concepts, financial agreements, national coordination, and a wartime escalation framework. Radiotherapy preparedness should be treated as a routine component of cancer care in unstable regions, not an emergency exercise begun only after treatment has already been interrupted.

papers.abstract: Social and emotional support (S&E support) is an underexamined determinant of cancer survivorship, and its interplay with food insecurity is poorly characterized. We sought to quantify inadequate S&E support and evaluate its independent and joint associations with food insecurity and health outcomes among cancer survivors. Using 2022-2023 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) data, 13,104 respondents with a history of cancer and 26,208 matched non-cancer controls were identified. Survey-weighted logistic regression models assessed associations between inadequate S&E support, food insecurity, and health outcomes, adjusting for sociodemographic and behavioral factors. Among 39,312 respondents, mean age was 67.1 years (SD 11.5), 60.1% (n = 23,700) were female and 77.2% (n = 32,979) identified as non-Hispanic White. Approximately half had annual household income ≥ $50,000 (54.6%, n = 16,604), never smoked (54.0%, n = 20,662), and reported no alcohol use (54.7%, n = 19,489). Among cancer survivors, respondents who were never married (aOR 1.74, 95%CI 1.12-2.69) or divorced/separated (aOR 1.75, 95%CI 1.25-2.46) had greater odds of inadequate S&E support, whereas higher income was protective ($50,000-$99,999: aOR 0.61, 95%CI 0.44-0.83; ≥$100,000: aOR 0.35, 95%CI 0.23-0.53). Inadequate S&E support was associated with higher odds of food insecurity (aOR 2.58, 95%CI 1.77-3.74), poor general health (aOR 2.78, 95%CI 2.13-3.62), poor physical health (aOR 1.95, 95%CI 1.48-2.57) and poor mental health (aOR 3.76, 95%CI 2.83-5.01). In stratified analysis, inadequate S&E support was linked with higher predicted probability of poor general health among food-secure (47.0%, 95%CI 41.2-52.9 vs. 27.3%, 95%CI 25.2-29.4) and food-insecure (54.5%, 95%CI 42.9-66.0 vs. 42.6%, 95%CI 33.2-52.0) cancer survivors. Inadequate S&E support clustered among socioeconomically disadvantaged cancer survivors and was independently associated with adverse health outcomes. Joint exposure to inadequate S&E support and food insecurity identified the poorest health profiles, supporting integrated psychosocial and material support in survivorship care.

papers.abstract: Pancreatic cancer (PC) commonly develops intrinsic or acquired resistance to gemcitabine (GEM), limiting clinical benefit. To uncover the underlying chromatin and transcriptional programs and identify actionable targets, we integrated ATAC-seq and RNA-seq in a GEM-resistant AsPC-1 subline (AsPC-1 GR) and parental cells. Although global chromatin accessibility decreased in AsPC-1 GR, a set of resistance-specific open regions (Peak_up) emerged. Integrating Peak_up with resistance-upregulated genes (DEG_up) identified 916 candidate resistance-associated genes, and motif analysis further narrowed the regulatory candidates to 23 core transcription factors, with EGR1 prioritized. EGR1 knockdown increased GEM sensitivity and reduced clonogenic growth, whereas EGR1 overexpression promoted survival and tumor growth and weakened GEM efficacy in xenografts. Mechanistically, EGR1 suppressed GEM-induced pyroptosis, with reduced LDH release and decreased IL-1β, consistent with inhibited caspase-1/GSDMD signaling. Multi-evidence integration identified 26 EGR1-linked resistance genes; TCGA survival analysis and validation highlighted SERPINB1 as a key downstream effector. SERPINB1 promoted GEM tolerance by restraining caspase-1 activation, GSDMD cleavage, and cytokine release, indicating inhibition of pyroptosis. Immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry revealed EGR1 interaction with WDR5, and WDR5/SET1A positively regulated SERPINB1. ChIP-seq data mining and ChIP-qPCR showed co-enrichment of EGR1, WDR5, SET1A, and H3K4me3 at the SERPINB1 promoter, supporting an EGR1-driven epigenetic activation model. Therapeutically, IT25, an inhibitor of EGR1 DNA-binding activity, downregulated SERPINB1, restored GEM-induced caspase-1/GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis, and enhanced the antitumor efficacy of GEM in vivo. Collectively, these findings identify the EGR1-WDR5/SET1A-H3K4me3-SERPINB1 axis as a key driver of GEM resistance in PC and suggest that IT25-based combination therapy may improve GEM efficacy by reactivating pyroptosis.

papers.abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic inflammatory central nervous system (CNS) disease. Although current immunotherapies control relapses, they have limited impact on progression, which might reflect incomplete access to or modulation of compartmentalized CNS inflammation. Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells can infiltrate tissues, but their ability to access and eliminate immune cells residing in the CNS remains elusive. We report the treatment of five individuals with progressive or relapsing-remitting MS with autologous CD19 CAR T cells to assess safety-relevant aspects, CNS bioavailability, and compartment-specific effects. The intervention induces remodeling of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) B cell pool, with a sustained reduction in CSF humoral biomarkers. Notably, CSF-infiltrating CAR T cells selectively upregulate phosphodiesterase 7B, while reconstituted peripheral B cells show altered cytokine and homing profiles. These findings indicate compartment-specific immunomodulation beyond peripheral B cell depletion and support controlled trials to test safety, durability, and efficacy.

papers.abstract: To report mature safety, urinary outcomes, PSA response, and biochemical control after 24-Gy single-dose radiotherapy (SDRT) versus 45 Gy in 5 fractions in two independently randomized PROSINT cohorts of intermediate-risk prostate cancer. This pooled analysis included 59 evaluable patients randomized locally (45 Gy/5 fractions, n=30; 24-Gy SDRT, n=29). Treatment-related safety was primary, anchored to grade ≥3 genitourinary (GU) or gastrointestinal (GI) events within 3 months (NCI CTCAE v4.0). Acute and late toxicity were ≤90 and >90 days after treatment, respectively. IPSS was modeled longitudinally using generalized estimating equations; PSA kinetics descriptively and biochemical relapse-free survival (bRFS) by Kaplan-Meier/Cox methods. The analysis was not designed for equivalence or noninferiority; efficacy analyses were exploratory. Median follow-up was 60.2 months. No treatment-related grade ≥3 GU or GI toxicity occurred (0/59; 95% CI, 0%-6.1%). Acute grade 1 GU toxicity was 53.3% with 45 Gy/5 fractions and 75.9% with SDRT (P=.103), and GI toxicity 10.0% and 24.1%, respectively (P=.181); no acute grade 2 events occurred. Late GU grade 1 toxicity was 36.7% with 45 Gy/5 fractions and 62.1% with SDRT (HR, 2.04; 95% CI, 0.96-4.32), whereas grade 2 remained uncommon (3.3% vs 10.3%; HR, 3.19; 95% CI, 0.33-30.71). Late GI toxicity was rare. Overall treatment-related grade ≥2 GU/GI toxicity was 6.8%/3.4%. Despite more frequent clinician-reported low-grade GU events after SDRT, IPSS increased transiently at 1 month and recovered toward baseline by 3 months in both arms; the between-arm difference in 1-month change was 2.7 points (95% CI, -1.80 to 7.16), with no evidence of differing longitudinal patterns (P=.733). PSA suppression was deep and sustained, with median PSA of 0.30 ng/mL after 45 Gy/5 fractions and 0.36 ng/mL after SDRT at 36 months. Eleven biochemical failures occurred (5 after 45 Gy/5 fractions; 6 after SDRT); 60-month bRFS was 85.1% (95% CI, 65.1%-94.2%) versus 80.5% (95% CI, 59.2%-91.5%) (HR, 1.05; 95% CI, 0.31-3.50). Clinically significant treatment-related toxicity was uncommon after both regimens. Low-grade GU events were more frequent after SDRT, while patient-reported urinary symptoms recovered toward baseline in both arms. PSA suppression was deep and sustained, but comparative disease-control estimates remained imprecise. These findings support continued prospective evaluation of 24-Gy SDRT with adequately powered disease-control endpoints.

papers.abstract: HEV infection is an underappreciated differential diagnosis in patients presenting with acute hepatitis during immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. As T-cells are the key targets of ICIs, particularly through blockade of inhibitory immune checkpoints such as PD-1, this intervention is likely to influence the dynamics and differentiation fate of de novo primed virus-specific T-cells during primary HEV infection. We therefore aimed to examine how PD-1 blockade during primary HEV-infection influences expansion, contraction, and memory formation of virus-specific CD8+ T-cells. HEV-specific CD8 and CD4+ T-cells were analyzed by applying a reverse phenotyping approach combined with single-cell transcriptomics and TCR sequencing, as well as multiparameter flow cytometry with MHC class I tetramers. We characterized HEV-specific T-cell responses in patients receiving ICI and in untreated patients during acute-viremic infection and after viral clearance. Under ICI, de novo primed HEV-specific CD8+ T-cells showed enhanced clonal expansion, cytotoxicity, and terminal differentiation. Rather than transitioning into classical memory subsets, these cells retained a cytotoxic transcriptional program and acquired features of long-lived effector-like T-cells (LLEC). While HEV-specific T-cells remained detectable over > 2 years, their functional recall responsiveness declined in ICI-treated patients. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that PD-1 blockade during the formation of a primary immune response reshapes the fate of the antiviral CD8+ T-cell pool, favoring terminally differentiated effector states over conventional memory formation, with potential implications for viral infections, vaccination, and immunotherapeutic strategies. Our study represents the first demonstration in a human model that PD-1 blockade during primary antigen exposure reshapes antiviral CD8+ T-cell effector formation and memory differentiation. By identifying PD-1 signaling during a primary immune response as a regulator of antiviral CD8+ T-cell fate, our findings establish a conceptual framework for understanding how immune checkpoint blockade influences the development of primary antiviral T-cell responses, with implications for viral infections, vaccination, and immunotherapeutic strategies.

papers.abstract: Cisplatin resistance critically limits muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) therapy, yet the underlying regulatory mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we report that NOP2, an RNA m5C methyltransferase, is upregulated in cisplatin-resistant bladder cancer cells and clinical tumor samples, correlating with poor chemotherapeutic response. Mechanistically, P300-catalyzed lactylation at NOP2 K772 disrupts its association with the E3 ligase PJA2, thereby evading K48-linked ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. Stabilized NOP2 deposits m5C modifications within the coding sequence of GLS1 mRNA, which are recognized by the reader YBX1 to enhance GLS1 transcript stability and translation. Elevated GLS1 reprograms glutamine metabolism, augments glutathione and NADPH pools, suppresses ferroptosis, and drives cisplatin resistance. Notably, genetic depletion of NOP2 or GLS1, or pharmacological targeting with the GLS1 inhibitor CB-839, restores cisplatin sensitivity and synergizes with the ferroptosis inducer RSL3 in vitro and in vivo. Our findings uncover a lactylation-dependent stabilization of NOP2 and define a NOP2-GLS1 epitranscriptomic-metabolic axis that links m5C remodeling to ferroptosis evasion in chemoresistant MIBC, suggesting that interrupting this cascade represents a viable therapeutic strategy to overcome cisplatin resistance.

papers.abstract: The 2025 UK Code of Practice revised adult death determination using neurological criteria, including requirements for temperature, apnoea testing, and other aspects of assessment. National audit data describe how often testing occurs and record reasons for non-testing, but do not establish the consistency, quality, or physiological consequences of individual assessments. Testing rates were declining before the revised Code, precluding simple attribution of that decline to its introduction. We propose prospective patient-level evaluation from a predefined clinical screening trigger through assessment to confirmation of death, identification of persisting brainstem function, circulatory death before completion or after withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment, or continued treatment. A proposed dataset combines assessment timelines, individual prerequisites, test results, successive barriers, physiological events, and clinician experience. These findings should distinguish inconsistent interpretation from difficulties arising despite correct implementation and identify priorities for clarification, training, or focused evidence review.

papers.abstract: General anaesthesia for Caesarean delivery is increasingly used as a quality indicator, but general anaesthesia rates alone are not measures of quality. The multinational anaesthesia practice for Caesarean delivery snapshot study demonstrates variation in general anaesthesia use across European centres, emphasising the need to interpret these rates within the systems in which anaesthetic decisions occur. We propose an interpretation framework based on three domains: access to appropriate neuraxial care, reliability of neuraxial techniques and rescue pathways, and patient experience. The rates of general anaesthesia for Caesarean delivery should prompt investigation of system capacity rather than serve as verdicts on quality or safety.

papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is one of the most devastating malignancies, with its incidence and mortality rates remaining particularly discouraging. Elucidating the molecular mechanisms driving PDAC progression and identifying potential therapeutic targets are critical to improve the clinical prognosis of PDAC patients. Accumulating evidence has highlighted the pivotal functions of centromere proteins (CENPs) in tumor progression. Accordingly, this study aimed to screen and identify key CENP family members implicated in PDAC pathogenesis. Through systematic analysis of CENP family proteins in PDAC, we identified CENPT as a critical regulator involved in disease progression. We further validated that CENPT promoted the proliferation and metastasis of PDAC cells via activating the RAF/MEK/ERK signaling pathway through a series of in vitro and in vivo experiments. In addition, CENPT was also found to be implicated in tumor microenvironment remodeling. Single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses demonstrated that CENPT expression was positively correlated with Treg cell abundance and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Further experiments suggested that CENPT upregulated the synthesis and secretion of MIF in PDAC cells, which acted on naive CD4+ T cells to promote the differentiation into Treg cells. This process ultimately induced the formation of an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and facilitated PDAC progression, whereas blockade of MIF enhanced the efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade for PDAC. In conclusion, this study revealed the crucial role of CENPT in PDAC progression, and targeting CENPT may serve as one of the potential therapeutic strategies for PDAC.

papers.abstract: This Matters Arising commentary addresses the recent article by Patidar et al. (2026) on TTK-mediated ceRNA networks in lung adenocarcinoma. We identify two critical scientific issues that are not addressed in the original paper's Limitations section. First, the authors interpret molecular docking scores as evidence of binding affinity and inhibitory activity, which is scientifically unsupported. Second, the therapeutic recommendation for hesperidin lacks any functional validation, as no enzymatic, cellular, or in vivo assays were performed. These concerns fundamentally affect the validity of the paper's therapeutic conclusions and warrant clarification.

papers.abstract: Genomic assays guide adjuvant treatment decisions in early-stage hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative (HR+/HER2-) breast cancer, yet contemporary treatment patterns and outcomes among premenopausal women remain incompletely characterized, particularly as adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitors enter routine use. We characterized adjuvant chemotherapy use and its association with overall survival (OS) in premenopausal women with early-stage HR+/HER2- breast cancer, stratified by Oncotype DX recurrence score (RS) and by eligibility for adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy. In this retrospective National Cancer Database (NCDB) analysis, we identified 19,419 premenopausal women (age < 50 years as a surrogate for menopausal status), diagnosed with stage I-III HR+/HER2-, clinically node-negative (including those pathologically node-positive) invasive breast cancer between 2018 and 2022. Primary and secondary exposures were adjuvant chemotherapy and CDK4/6 inhibitor eligibility. The primary outcome was OS. Cox proportional hazards models with robust variance were adjusted a priori for age, RS, and positive lymph nodes, with additional RS-stratified analyses. Overall, 13,490 women (69.5%) received no adjuvant chemotherapy. Chemotherapy receipt rose with genomic risk and CDK4/6 inhibitor eligibility, while OncotypeDX testing was least frequent in the highest-risk groups. Adjuvant chemotherapy was independently associated with improved OS overall (adjusted HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.47-0.86). In RS-stratified analyses, the association was limited to RS 21-25 (aHR 0.24, 95% CI 0.08-0.68) and unknown RS (aHR 0.61, 95% CI 0.42-0.89). Adjuvant chemotherapy was associated with improved OS, mostly among RS 21-25 and a higher-risk unknown-RS group. Frequent absence of genomic testing among CDK4/6 inhibitor-eligible women highlights an opportunity to better integrate genomic and clinical-anatomic risk in treatment selection.

papers.abstract: Liver resections involving the hepato-caval confluence and/or retrohepatic inferior vena cava (IVC) sometimes require standard total vascular exclusion (TVE) with hypothermic perfusion. Veno-venous bypass (VVB) supports hemodynamic stability during TVE, but conventional external VVB carries risks including bleeding, air embolism, hemodynamic instability, hypothermia, and cannulation-site complications. Internal bypass alternatives have been described in liver transplantation but not previously in liver resection. We describe a novel internal porto-cavo-caval VVB technique-cavo-caval shunt (CCS) combined with temporary portocaval shunt (PCS)-performed during liver resection under standard TVE with hypothermic perfusion. The IVC is fully mobilized and lengthened via diaphragmatic hiatus opening; a reinforced PTFE graft is anastomosed laterally to the supra- and infrahepatic IVC, with a temporary PCS graft connecting the caval and portal systems. In one case, a pre-fashioned Y-shaped graft was used to reduce the number of anastomoses. The technique was applied in three patients undergoing extended hepatectomy for cholangiocarcinoma (n = 2) and alveolar hydatid disease (n = 1). TVE durations ranged from 90 to 120 min. All three procedures were completed without hemodynamic instability or complications attributable to the cavo-caval shunt. Postoperative courses included manageable complications unrelated to the bypass technique. All patients survived to discharge and remain alive at last follow-up. Internal porto-cavo-caval VVB via CCS with temporary PCS is a feasible alternative to external bypass during complex liver resection requiring standard TVE, preserving hepatic protection and bloodless exposure while avoiding external cannulation-related morbidity and core hypothermia.

papers.abstract: Anatomical resection of posterosuperior liver segments remains technically demanding because of the deep operative field, proximity to major hepatic veins, and variable Glissonean pedicle anatomy. We describe a robotic strategy integrating preoperative three-dimensional (3D) planning, hepatic vein-guided navigation, and indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence guidance. Resection was performed using the da Vinci 5 platform with four arms. Preoperative 3D reconstruction were used to identify the target Glissonean pedicles, the dorsal branch of the segment 8 pedicle (G8d) and the segment 7 pedicle (G7) and to define their spatial relationships with the RHV and IRHV, respectively. The strategy comprised three sequential steps: (1) a cranial approach to the RHV with G8d dissection; (2) a dorsal approach to the IRHV with G7 dissection; and (3) ICG fluorescence demarcation of the ischemic boundary followed by fluorescence-guided parenchymal transection. A 39-year-old woman underwent resection of a posterosuperior liver mass. Operative time was 220 min, estimated blood loss was 50 mL, and no transfusion was required. Pathology confirmed hepatocellular carcinoma arising in a hepatocellular adenoma. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 6 without complications. Robotic anatomical resection of segment 7 and the segment 8 dorsal area was feasible and safely completed using this structured strategy. Integration of 3D planning, hepatic vein-guided navigation, and ICG fluorescence may improve anatomical precision and reduce inadvertent vascular injury or incomplete anatomical transection in complex posterosuperior resections.

papers.abstract: After outpatient breast surgery, opioids are routinely prescribed in far greater quantity than patients consume, leaving a preventable reservoir of leftover pills at risk for misuse and diversion. This study evaluated a preoperative educational intervention and assessed whether opioid prescribing after outpatient breast surgical oncology (BSO) operations aligns with actual consumption and patient preference. In this prospective quality improvement study, patients undergoing outpatient BSO operations (n = 227) at a single cancer center from October 2025 through May 2026 received a preoperative storage and disposal handout and completed a postoperative survey. Prescriptions followed Overdose Prevention Engagement Network guidelines. Opioids were converted to oral morphine equivalents (OMEs). The primary comparison was prescribed versus consumed OMEs, assessed overall and across five surgical groups, together with retrospective patient preference, storage, and disposal. The median OME prescribed was 50 (IQR, 30-100) compared with 5 (IQR, 0-25) consumed (P < 0.001). Prescribing increased with the extent of surgery, whereas consumption remained low across all groups. In retrospect, 62% of the patients preferred fewer opioids. Two thirds stored opioids properly, exceeding historical rates, whereas disposal was uncommon at follow-up evaluation (7%), although most of the patients intended to dispose. A gap between opioids prescribed and consumed persisted despite prescribing concordant with national guidelines, and most patients preferred fewer opioids in retrospect. A brief educational intervention was associated with favorable storage but limited early disposal. These findings support prospective protocols that individualize opioid prescribing and reinforce disposal after outpatient breast operations.

papers.abstract: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) is increasingly used in locally advanced gallbladder cancer (LAGBC), achieving pathological complete response (pCR) in some patients. We investigated factors predicting pCR and its impact on survival. This observational cohort study assessed all consecutive patients with LAGBC undergoing curative resection after NACT, from January 2015 to December 2022. We assessed pCR incidence (absence of viable tumor cells in the sampled gallbladder and lymph node), associated factors, and survival outcomes. In total, 86 patients were included in the final analysis. The Mandard tumor regression score was evaluable in 83 patients; 11 of these patients (13.25%) experienced pCR. Although patients with pCR had the best survival, pathological responders (Mandard grades 1-2) demonstrated better overall survival (median not reached) than the 32 months for poor responders (Mandard 3-5) (p = 0.048). Responders had disease-free survival of 31 months versus 9.2 months for poor responders (p = 0.057). Neither the multiagent chemotherapy nor number of cycles correlated with pathological response. pCR was achieved in 13.25% of patients with LAGBC after NACT. Although patients with pCR fared best, graded pathological response correlated with improved overall survival and DFS. Identifying factors that predict pCR has implications for treatment strategies and warrants investigation in larger prospective studies.

papers.abstract: Ionizing radiation from medical imaging may increase brain tumor risk. To quantify brain tumor risk associated with radiation exposure from medical imaging in children and adolescents. Retrospective cohort study of children born from 1996 through 2016 who were enrolled from birth in 6 US health care systems or Ontario, Canada, and were alive and cancer-free at age 2 years, with follow-up through December 31, 2017 (US sites), and December 31, 2024 (Ontario). Cumulative radiation dose to the brain from medical imaging, lagged by 2 years. Incident brain or other central nervous system tumors. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models for categorical dose, and excess relative risks (ERRs) were estimated using linear dose-response models for continuous dose. Among 3 704 860 children (1 900 285 [51.3%] male) followed up for 45 671 641 person-years (mean follow-up, 12.3 years), 1536 brain tumors were diagnosed. Mean radiation dose from 1 head computed tomography (CT) examination was 66.2 mGy (SD, 22.2). Among children with cumulative dose of 1 mGy or greater, mean cumulative dose was 73 mGy (SD, 95) overall and 100 mGy (SD, 105) among those diagnosed with brain tumors. Compared with no exposure, brain tumor risk increased with cumulative dose (>0 to <1 mGy: HR, 1.12 [95% CI, 1.01-1.26]; 1 to <5 mGy: HR, 1.71 [95% CI, 0.88-2.96]; 5 to <50 mGy: HR, 1.86 [95% CI, 1.16-2.81]; 50 to <75 mGy: HR, 2.30 [95% CI, 1.64-3.12]; 75 to <100 mGy: HR, 2.02 [95% CI, 1.13-3.30]; 100 to <150 mGy: HR, 2.81 [95% CI, 1.53-4.66]; ≥150 mGy: HR, 3.85 [95% CI, 2.43-5.75]). Cumulative dose was associated with brain tumor risk overall (ERR per 100 mGy, 1.27 [95% CI, 0.83-1.77]; P < .001), with stronger associations for aggressive histologies (ERR per 100 mGy, 1.51 [95% CI, 1.00-2.11]; P < .001). By age 21 years, exposure comparable to 1 head CT was associated with 7.9 excess brain tumors per 10 000 children, or approximately 1 excess tumor per 1266 head CT examinations. The estimated population-attributable fraction was 10.1% (95% CI, 5.8%-14.2%). Medical imaging in children and adolescents was associated with a dose-related increase in brain tumor risk. These findings support careful clinical justification and dose minimization when pediatric imaging using ionizing radiation is indicated.

papers.abstract: CAR-T cells have yet to show widespread efficacy in solid tumors due in part to poor persistence and dysfunction in the tumor microenvironment. Further, heterogenous expression of target antigens can lead to escape of antigen-null tumors that resist CAR-T killing. Strategies to cooperatively boost both CAR-T and endogenous antitumor immunity may be critical for achieving durable efficacy in cancer patients. NKTR-255 is a polymer-conjugated IL-15 with extended half-life that can boost endogenous T and NK cells, as well as CD19 CAR-T cells in B cell malignancies. However, whether NKTR-255 is sufficient to overcome CAR-T dysfunction in the suppressive solid tumor microenvironment, and how NKTR-255 and CAR-Ts together re-shape endogenous antitumor immunity, is not known. Using mouse models of ROR1+ lung adenocarcinoma, we show that NKTR-255 significantly boosted accumulation and function of tumor-infiltrating CAR-T cells targeting ROR1. Compared with NKTR-255 or CAR-T treatment alone, combination of NKTR-255 and CAR-T therapy increased endogenous tumor-specific T cells that preserved a PD-1+Tcf1+ stem-like phenotype. Consequently, NKTR-255 and CAR-T combination therapy completely eliminated ROR1+ tumor cells and significantly improved survival, with enhanced tumor control dependent on both CAR-Ts and endogenous T cells, though all mice ultimately succumbed to progression of ROR1- tumor. Compared to IL-15-armored CAR-T cells, systemic NKTR-255 induced greater accumulation and reduced terminal differentiation of endogenous tumor-specific T cells, resulting in superior tumor control. Thus, combining NKTR-255 with CAR-T therapy is a promising strategy to enhance both CAR-T and endogenous antitumor immunity to promote coordinated control of aggressive tumors.

papers.abstract: Cancer stem cells (CSC) are a small group of tumor cells capable of self-renewing, giving rise to new tumors, and resisting treatment, thereby causing recurrence and metastasis and representing a serious clinical problem. However, there are no approved therapies for their elimination, and limited information is available on the effects of current therapies on tumor stemness. A general consensus suggests that the anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment promotes tumor stemness. Since we previously reported that ablation of the p50 NF-κB gene in the hematopoietic compartment (p50fl/flTie2-Cre mice) restores M1/Th1 antitumor immunity, we studied its effects on CSC and therapy resistance in models of fibrosarcoma and melanoma. Using p50fl/flTie2-Cre mice, we demonstrate that p50 NF-κB silencing impairs CSC development, their migratory capacity, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), events known to correlate with tumor aggressiveness. Furthermore, we identify a clear antagonistic effect between Th1 and Th2 T cell polarization, with the former acting as inhibitors and the latter promoting the stemness phenotype. Consistently, while immunotherapy with anti-PD-1 promoted a marked reduction in CSC and tumor development, associated with increased levels of IFNγ, whereas concomitant administration of anti-IFNγ antibodies restored tumor growth and dissemination. Moreover, treatment with anti-IL-4 enhanced the antitumor effects of immunotherapy, reducing tumor cell stemness. Importantly, the antitumor effects of high-dose IFNγ and anti-IL-4 were confirmed in combination with doxorubicin chemotherapy. Overall, our data indicate that shifting the immune response toward a robust M1/Th1 state can significantly improve current immunotherapies and chemotherapies, by limiting CSC properties.

papers.abstract: Long-term lung cancer (LC) survivors remain at risk of LC events (LCEs), including late recurrence and second primary LC, beyond 5 years after diagnosis, but the role of computed tomography (CT) surveillance beyond 5 years remains uncertain. To evaluate whether CT receipt beyond 5 years after LC diagnosis is associated with LCEs and survival. This nationwide population-based cohort study used sequential target trial emulation with monthly eligibility reassessment and time-updated propensity score matching based on data from the Korean National Health Insurance Service database. Patients diagnosed with LC from 2006 to 2019 were followed up through December 31, 2024. Long-term LC survivors were eligible for trial entry 5.5 years after diagnosis if they had no administrative evidence of active or recurrent LC, a prior LCE, or another primary cancer. Data were analyzed between January 1, 2026, and February 28, 2026. CT receipt beyond 5 years after LC diagnosis, defined as chest CT during the 1-month assessment window at each monthly trial baseline, compared with no CT receipt. The primary outcome was LCE occurrence, defined by new LC-specific special copayment registration after the monthly trial baseline. Secondary outcomes were all-cause mortality, surgical resection after LCE detection, and subsequent mortality. The cohort of 55 694 LC survivors (mean [SD] age, 63.3 [10.9] years; 58.0% male) contributed 2 629 462 eligible person-trials. Matching yielded 583 756 person-trials per group. During a median (IQR) follow-up of 2.74 (1.16-5.18) years, CT receipt was associated with a higher incidence of LCEs (2.49% vs 1.97% per year; hazard ratio [HR], 1.28 [95% CI, 1.26-1.29]) and lower all-cause mortality rate (2.62% vs 4.33% per year; HR, 0.66 [95% CI, 0.65-0.67]) compared with no CT receipt. Among patients with an LCE, CT receipt was associated with greater odds of surgical resection after LCE (odds ratio, 1.46 [95% CI, 1.41-1.52]) and a lower subsequent mortality risk (HR, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.61-0.64]). These associations were observed more frequently among females (HR, 0.47 [95% CI, 0.44-0.49]), older adults (HR, 0.57 [95% CI, 0.54-0.60]), and never smokers (HR, 0.55 [95% CI, 0.53-0.57]). In this cohort study, CT receipt beyond 5 years after LC diagnosis was associated with increased detection of LCEs, greater use of surgical resection after an LCE, and a lower all-cause mortality rate. These findings support further evaluation of risk-adapted CT surveillance beyond 5 years in selected LC survivors.

papers.abstract: Lung cancer screening with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) has been shown to identify lung cancers at earlier stages and to significantly reduce lung cancer mortality in prior randomized clinical trials. However, the benefit of LDCT screening for small cell lung cancer (SCLC), an aggressive subtype of lung cancer, is unclear. To investigate the characteristics and outcomes of SCLC diagnosed after a lung cancer screening examination using a large database of Medicare beneficiaries. In this retrospective cohort study, Medicare data linked to the Surveillance Epidemiology End Results Program's cancer registry data were analyzed. Patients in the US aged 65 to 78 years who were diagnosed with SCLC from 2015 to 2021 were identified for analysis, with follow-up data through 2022. Patients who underwent 1 or more LDCT lung cancer screening examinations during the 12 months preceding their SCLC diagnosis were included in the screened group. All other patients were included in the unscreened group. Data were analyzed from January to August 2026. One or more LDCT lung cancer screenings during the 12 months preceding SCLC diagnosis. The primary outcomes were stage at SCLC diagnosis and overall survival after SCLC diagnosis in the screened and unscreened groups. A total of 17 099 patients (median [IQR] age, 72.0 [69.0-75.0] years; 8999 [52.6%] female) met study inclusion criteria, of which 949 (5.5%) were included in the screened group and 16 150 (94.5%) were included in the unscreened group. When compared with patients in the unscreened group, patients in the screened group were significantly less likely to be diagnosed with distant disease (419 of 949 [44.2%] vs 11 376 of 16 150 [70.4%]; P < .001). Patients in the screened group also had significantly better overall survival when compared with patients in the unscreened group (3-year overall survival, 28.0% [95% CI, 24.9%-31.2%] vs 10.8% [95% CI, 10.3%-11.3%]; P < .001). Both findings were consistent in propensity score-matched analysis. Results of this cohort study of Medicare beneficiaries diagnosed with SCLC suggest that receipt of lung cancer screening was associated with a shift toward earlier-stage SCLC at diagnosis and improved overall survival.

papers.abstract: NRG Oncology RTOG 9902 was a randomized controlled trial of the addition of adjuvant chemotherapy (paclitaxel, oral etoposide, estramustine) to long-course androgen suppression and radiation for patients with high-risk prostate cancer. The trial closed early due to excess toxicity and found no benefit to chemotherapy at a median follow-up of 9.2 years. Immediate post-radiation PSA status was dichotomized at ≤ 0.2 ng/mL. Landmark analysis redefined starting times for disease-free survival (DFS), time to distant metastasis (TDM), and overall survival (OS) at 36 weeks post-radiation, when planned chemotherapy was complete. Exclusion criteria included non-receipt of radiation or assigned chemotherapy and pre-landmark DFS events or loss to follow-up. Hazard ratios (HR), 95% confidence intervals, and PSA-by-treatment interaction estimated by Cox or competing-risks regression. Of 333 patients analyzed: 190 without and 143 with chemotherapy. Chemotherapy was associated with improved DFS for patients with PSA > 0.2 (HR 0.59, 0.38-0.91), but not for those with PSA ≤ 0.2 (HR 0.94, 0.60-1.46), interaction p = 0.13. There was no association with chemotherapy relative to post-RT PSA for either TDM or OS. This analysis suggests that men with a post-radiation PSA > 0.2 may benefit from treatment intensification with adjuvant chemotherapy. Prospective trials adapting treatment by PSA response are indicated. Trial Number: NCT00004054 (ClinicalTrials.gov).

papers.abstract: Insulin-like growth factor (IGF) signaling drives progression of glioblastoma (GBM), the most aggressive brain cancer. While sphingolipid metabolism is implicated in gliomagenesis, the mechanism by which it regulates GBM growth and therapy response is poorly understood. Through bioinformatic analyses of human gliomas, we identified sphingolipid metabolism genes with potential functional significance in glioma. Using patient-derived cells, a Drosophila glioma model, and xenograft mouse models, we investigated the functional role of Dihydroceramide desaturase 1 (DEGS1). Lipidomics profiling and RNA sequencing were performed in patient-derived cells to reveal the mechanism by which DEGS1 regulates glioma growth. Additionally, we tested the effect of a DEGS1 inhibitor on GBM cell growth and their resistance to IGF1R-targeted therapy. Our data demonstrate that the expression of sphingolipid metabolism gene DEGS1 is associated with aggressive glioma biomarkers and worse patient survival. DEGS1 is required for glioma growth in patient-derived cells, a Drosophila glioma model, and xenograft mouse models. Lipidomics profiling reveals that DEGS1 deficiency results in reduced ceramides and complex sphingolipids and accumulation of their precursors. Disrupted sphingolipid homeostasis impairs lipid raft biogenesis and lipid raft-associated IGF signaling. Targeting DEGS1 decreases GBM cell growth and their resistance to IGF1R inhibition. These findings establish that targeting DEGS1-regulated sphingolipid metabolism is a viable avenue to inhibit IGF signaling-driven GBM growth.

papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) develops in a nutrient-poor microenvironment and progresses from pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia (PanIN) to invasive carcinoma. Serine metabolism supports tumor growth in many cancers, spurring the development of inhibitors of phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PHGDH), the rate-limiting enzyme in serine biosynthesis. However, the limited clinical success of PHGDH inhibitors highlights the need to better understand the stage-specific role of de novo serine synthesis during PDAC progression. Here, we showed that PHGDH increases progressively from PanIN to invasive PDAC in human and mouse tissues. In genetically engineered mouse models with inducible PHGDH knockdown, PHGDH loss delayed PDAC development. Acute treatment with the PHGDH inhibitor BI-9593 suppressed de novo serine synthesis, induced cell death, and drove tumor regression. Unexpectedly, PHGDH-deficient tumors did not become more dependent on exogenous serine, and dietary serine/glycine manipulation did not affect tumor development. Instead, stable isotope tracing and metabolomic profiling showed that PHGDH loss reduced ASCT2 expression and impaired glutamine uptake and utilization, creating a metabolic liability that rendered PHGDH-deficient tumors selectively sensitive to the glutamine antagonist DRP-104. Together, these findings reveal a therapeutic vulnerability to combined metabolic targeting in PDAC.

papers.abstract: Tissue injury is a pervasive feature of human disease, yet adult mammals exhibit limited regenerative capacity. A central determinant of regenerative outcomes is the inflammatory response, which orchestrates tissue repair through mechanisms that are evolutionarily conserved from Drosophila to mammals. Following injury, inflammation drives debris clearance, promotes the release of cytokines and growth factors, and contributes to the restoration of functional cells. However, dysregulated or unresolved inflammation can impair healing, drive scar formation, and ultimately result in organ dysfunction or failure. Here, we focus on recent advances in the spatiotemporal regulation of inflammation during tissue repair that have reshaped our understanding of its underlying mechanisms. We synthesize findings on the dynamic progression of repair from inflammatory initiation to active resolution and stem cell activation, highlighting features of immune cell plasticity and heterogeneity within injury-specific microenvironments, as well as the existence of pivotal macrophage-fibroblast interactions. Furthermore, we delineate the pleiotropic and context-dependent roles of key cytokines and signaling pathways in coordinating these processes. Finally, we discuss current and emerging therapeutic strategies, emphasizing the paradigm shift from broad immunosuppression toward precise modulation of inflammatory networks to promote regeneration and prevent fibrosis. Future progress hinges on integrating multiomic spatial atlases, precision immunomodulation, and standardized therapeutic protocols to decipher and manipulate immune-regenerative crosstalk, thereby driving the development of next-generation regenerative therapies.

papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of treatment response remains challenging in cancer. To facilitate response prediction in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), we developed PRISM, an interpretable multiscale graph-learning framework for estimating treatment-specific objective response from pretreatment H&E whole-slide images. PRISM integrated multiresolution tissue representations with a cell-level tumor microenvironment (TME) hypergraph, thereby treating higher-order microenvironmental organization as a learnable component of treatment-response prediction. Samples from 7,082 patients from four Chinese centers were screened. PRISM was evaluated across treatment specific cohorts receiving targeted therapy (T), EGFR-targeted therapy (T_EGFR), immune checkpoint inhibitor-based therapy (ICI), chemoimmunotherapy (CI), and chemotherapy (C) using patient-level internal cross-validation, independent multicenter external validation, and prospective silent validation. PRISM predicted early objective responses across prespecified systemic therapies in NSCLC. In comparison to 18 established multiple-instance learning and computational pathology baseline models, PRISM remained competitive, with numerical advantages in selected tasks. Multiscale attribution and exploratory H&E-derived TME analyses provided spatial context for model predictions. Overall, PRISM offers a morphology-based framework for estimating early response to prespecified systemic therapies and warrants further prospective multicenter evaluation.

papers.abstract: Resistance to PD-1-based immunotherapy remains a major challenge in cancer treatment, especially in immunologically "cold" tumors characterized by T-cell exclusion and impaired T-cell effector function. Mechanical processes impact T-cell activity, and mechanical perturbations may represent a distinct mode of immune suppression. Here, we identified CD209, a myeloid-expressed C-type lectin receptor, as a mechanosuppressive regulator of antitumor T-cell immunity. CD209 was selectively enriched in tumor-infiltrating M2-like macrophages and monocytes, and elevated CD209 expression was associated with poor clinical response to PD-1 blockade and immune dysfunction and exclusion across multiple cancer types. Mechanistically, CD209 directly engaged ICAM-2 on T cells and activated ROCK1-ERM signaling. This interaction increased T-cell cortical stiffness, destabilized T cell-antigen presenting cell interactions, and attenuated T-cell receptor signaling. Blocking the CD209-ICAM-2-ERM pathway restored T-cell activation and promoted CD8+ T-cell infiltration and effector function in both in vivo mouse models and ex vivo human tumor systems. Importantly, CD209 blockade enhanced the response to PD-1 inhibition and overcame resistance to PD-1-based immunotherapy in refractory and immunologically "cold" tumor models. Together, these findings define a myeloid-derived mechanical immune checkpoint and reveal T-cell mechanosuppression as a targetable mechanism of tumor immune evasion and immunotherapy resistance.

papers.abstract: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) measures cortical hemodynamics, yet its ability to characterize anesthesia-related functional changes remains unclear. This exploratory secondary analysis used prospectively collected data from 120 female patients undergoing gynecologic laparoscopic surgery under propofol or sevoflurane anesthesia (60 per group). Twenty-channel prefrontal fNIRS recordings covered wakefulness, induction, and maintenance. Deoxygenated hemoglobin-derived amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations (ALFF), functional connectivity (FC), network topology, and within- and cross-state FC similarity were assessed. Support vector machine, logistic regression, and random forest classifiers assessed discrimination between states. During induction, ALFF increased by 89.8% to 202.2% with propofol and 75.2% to 242.0% with sevoflurane across five prefrontal regions (all P < 0.001). During maintenance, mean ALFF was below awake levels, with significant reductions of 20.0% to 40.1% in three regions under sevoflurane (all P ≤ 0.019). Induction-related FC changes were limited and regionally heterogeneous. Regional FC, modularity, and global efficiency showed no significant maintenance-versus-awake differences in either group. Within-state between-subject FC similarity was significantly higher during maintenance than during wakefulness only with sevoflurane (mean difference [MD], 0.110; 95% CI, 0.054 to 0.169; P < 0.001). Cross-state between-subject FC similarity was higher for awake-maintenance than awake-induction comparisons with propofol (MD, 0.072; 95% CI, 0.055 to 0.090) and sevoflurane (MD, 0.144; 95% CI, 0.126 to 0.161; both P < 0.001). Support vector machine classification of induction versus wakefulness yielded areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.83 (95% CI, 0.75 to 0.90) for propofol and 0.85 (95% CI, 0.78 to 0.91) for sevoflurane; maintenance-versus-awake AUCs were 0.67 (95% CI, 0.58 to 0.75) and 0.76 (95% CI, 0.68 to 0.85). Prefrontal fNIRS detected widespread induction-related hemodynamic changes, but the present connectivity measures provided limited discrimination between maintenance of anesthesia and wakefulness.

papers.abstract: Pediatric B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) remains a major clinical challenge driven by molecular heterogeneity and therapeutic resistance. While the SWI/SNF chromatin-remodeling complex is a recognized dependency in myeloid and T-cell leukemias, its role in B-ALL remains poorly defined. Here, we identify a conserved requirement for the SWI/SNF ATPases SMARCA4 and SMARCA2 across diverse B-ALL genetic subtypes. SMARCA4 expression correlates with inferior overall survival in the pediatric B-ALL TARGET cohort. Using a panel of B-ALL models representing ETV6-RUNX1, BCR-ABL1, and KMT2A-rearranged subtypes, we show that dual SMARCA2/4 inhibition, using the ATPase inhibitor BRM014 or the PROTAC degrader ACBI1, induces profound loss of viability. This vulnerability is characterized by G0/G1 cell cycle arrest and a robust apoptotic response. Mechanistically, comparative RNA sequencing identified a high-confidence 26-gene "identity core" consistently downregulated upon SWI/SNF disruption with BRM014. This program integrates lymphocyte activation, cytokine signaling, and trafficking modules, including the key niche-interaction receptor CXCR4, and is accompanied by depletion of MYC and E2F transcriptional programs. Finally, BRM014 demonstrated significant growth-inhibitory activity in vivo in an REH xenograft model, with a significant delay in disease progression during the observation window. These findings establish the SWI/SNF complex as a conserved survival dependency in the tested B-ALL models and provide a rationale for targeting SMARCA2/4 to inhibit intrinsic growth in B-ALL.

papers.abstract: Brain neoplasms cause substantial morbidity and mortality in low- and middle-income countries, yet structural and geographic factors in access and outcomes are poorly quantified. Using discharge data from Mexico's Ministry of Health hospitals, we examined access to brain tumor surgery and the relationship between facility level and mortality. We retrospectively analyzed patients undergoing brain tumor surgery in Ministry of Health hospitals using the national discharge registry (2010-2022). Multivariable logistic regression with hospital-clustered standard errors assessed associations of facility level and travel time with in-hospital mortality, adjusting for clinical and socioeconomic covariates. We also examined timely access among patients and in the population. Among 10,532 patients, 74.4% reached care within 2 h, and 68.0% of the population lived within 2 h of a Ministry of Health level 3 neurosurgical center, below the 80% Lancet Commission benchmark. Indigenous community, pediatric age, and male sex were associated with lower odds of timely access. Surgery at a level 2 versus level 3 hospital was associated with higher in-hospital mortality (OR 1.25; 95% CI 1.01-1.56; sensitivity range 1.22-1.40), and travel time, less consistently, with a modest increase (OR 1.04 per hour beyond 2 h; 95% CI 1.00-1.07). Malignancy, older age, and pediatric age were associated with higher mortality. Within Mexico's Ministry of Health hospitals, brain tumor surgery is geographically concentrated, and surgery at level 2 hospitals was associated with higher in-hospital mortality. These findings warrant evaluation of level 2 neurosurgical capacity and referral pathways to tertiary centers.

papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, largely due to tumor heterogeneity, late diagnosis, and high recurrence rates even after curative treatment. Although HCC is potentially curable when detected at an early stage, suboptimal surveillance, particularly in patients with underlying cirrhosis or metabolic risk factors, limits the proportion of patients eligible for curative therapies. Current surveillance strategies for at-risk populations have intrinsic limitations, and the performance of imaging and serum biomarkers remains suboptimal. Moreover, the lack of reliable prognostic biomarkers for detecting early recurrence hampers post-treatment surveillance and impacts clinical outcomes. In this context, circulating biomarkers have emerged as promising tools for improving both early detection and prognostic stratification. Liquid biopsy has the potential to enable early, non-invasive diagnosis of HCC and allows longitudinal assessment of tumor progression through serial sampling. In early-stage HCC, blood candidates may complement or outperform conventional approaches by enabling earlier diagnosis and more accurate risk stratification. In this review, we summarize recent advances and current challenges in the clinical translation of circulating biomarkers. We focus on key liquid biopsy components, including circulating cell-free DNA, particularly circulating tumor DNA, circulating tumor cells, non-coding RNAs, extracellular vesicles, proteins and metabolites, such as bile acids and lipids, highlighting their diagnostic and prognostic potential and their possible integration into personalized management strategies for patients with early-stage HCC.

papers.abstract: Cancer incidence continues to increase globally, with many patients diagnosed during working age. Employment disruption after cancer diagnosis is an important survivorship and socioeconomic issue, yet long-term evidence across cancer types and patient subgroups remains limited. This study evaluated unemployment risk and workforce attrition among workers after cancer diagnosis. We conducted a nationwide cohort study of workers aged 18 to 60 years newly diagnosed with cancer between 2011 and 2020, with follow-up of up to 12 years. Noncancer workers were selected using 1:1 hybrid matching based on demographic, clinical, and insurance characteristics. The primary outcome was unemployment, defined as transition from employee status to dependent or local administrative enrollment without dependent eligibility for at least 12 months. Workforce attrition, defined as unemployment or death, was evaluated as a secondary outcome. Competing risk and Cox regression models were applied. After matching, 119,200 pairs of cancer and noncancer workers were included. The cumulative incidence of unemployment among cancer workers was 7.9% at 1 year and 32.5% at 12 years, compared with 5.3% and 22.9% among noncancer workers. Cancer diagnosis was associated with higher unemployment risk (subdistribution hazard ratio, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.48 to 1.54). Risks were greatest among women, individuals aged 40 to 49 years, and those with advanced-stage disease. Cancer was also associated with an approximately threefold higher risk of workforce attrition. Cancer diagnosis was associated with substantial long-term employment disruption. These findings highlight the need for survivorship-oriented workforce support and employment protection strategies.

papers.abstract: Tailgut cysts are rare congenital retrorectal lesions. Because the risk of malignancy remains uncertain, resection has historically been recommended even for asymptomatic patients. We examined whether clinical and imaging features can identify patients suitable for active surveillance. Patients diagnosed with a tailgut cyst at a tertiary cancer center between 1996 and 2021 were identified from radiology and pathology databases. Demographic, clinical, imaging, operative, pathologic, and oncologic data were reviewed. Management was individualized after multidisciplinary review. Survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Fifty-four patients were included; 47 (87%) had benign disease and 7 (13%) had malignant disease. Malignancy was present at diagnosis in all cases and occurred exclusively in symptomatic patients. Malignancy was associated with older age (median 57 vs. 45 years, p = 0.036) and rectal pain at presentation (86% vs. 30%, p = 0.008). On imaging, malignant cysts were significantly larger and more likely to demonstrate solid components, calcifications, and adjacent structure involvement. Twenty patients with benign-appearing cysts were enrolled in active surveillance. In this cohort, no malignant events were observed during follow-up, with a 5-year cancer-free survival of 100%. Five-year overall survival was 28.6% for malignant versus 91.9% for benign cysts (p < 0.0001). Malignant tailgut cysts appear to represent a clinically and radiographically distinct subset present at diagnosis. Asymptomatic patients with benign-appearing cysts demonstrated excellent long-term outcomes under active surveillance. These findings suggest that a risk-adapted management strategy incorporating symptoms and imaging features may help guide selection between surgery and surveillance.
